Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The procurement/legal team here at Solstice has asked for a concise technical mapping and a short justification for why Redwood's controls meet DPF requirements for our EU->US processing flows. They specifically want: 1) a diagram of export paths and where keys are held, 2) confirmation of encryption-at-rest keys (KMS/HSM), 3) retention and log-access scoping, and 4) a short paragraph we can paste into our DPA annex that explains fallback/failover routing to US regions.

I attached the RFP excerpt with their exact questions. Can you confirm if Redwood can provide a single-sheet mapping + a one-page justification by EOD Thursday? If not, propose the nearest feasible timeline. We may need to loop in your legal ops for DPA wording.

Appreciate it —
Sarah

Laura / Mateo / Sarah — quick ops details to feed into the mapping and paragraph:
- KMS: Redwood offers Redwood-managed KMS by default (AES-256) with customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated and Private customers via our KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM-backed key storage is supported in our Private on-prem package and Dedicated enterprise tiers (require add-on).
- Rotation: default 90-day rotation for symmetric keys; rotation events are logged to our audit log (immutable, WORM) and surfaced in Console > Security > Key events.
- Retention / Logs: retention for application logs is configurable by controller up to 7 years; audit logs are retained per contract but can be exported to customer S3/GCS on request.
- Fallback routing: our routing policy supports region-based preferences; if EU capacity is constrained we fallback to nearest compatible region in our US cluster with automatic cache invalidation and documented notification events (we can include example runbook).

I'll update the mapping workbook to include these rows and add a short ops note for each bullet.

Marissa
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
